major_risks: Total extent of the land is missing — cannot verify actual area of Survey No. 117, Hissa No. 1
Cultivable extent is not recorded — unable to determine productive portion
Kharab (uncultivable) extent is missing — potential undisclosed unusable land
Assessment (land revenue) value is blank — raises doubts about record completeness
Owner name is not mentioned — ownership cannot be verified from Akarband alone
positive_findings: Land classification is 'Dry / ಖುಷ್ಕಿ' (private agricultural), not government or forest land
Property is clearly identified by village (ಹುಪುಹ), hobli (ಸಾತನೂರು), taluk (ಕನಕಪುರ), and district (ರಾಮನಗರ)
reasoning: Akarband is a foundational revenue record; missing extent, assessment, and owner fields significantly reduce its evidentiary value.
While the Dry classification suggests private cultivable land (not government), the absence of extent and kharab details prevents verification of the saleable area.
Missing owner name means buyer must rely entirely on RTC/Mutation records for ownership proof — a documentation gap.
Per guidelines: missing total extent → MEDIUM; missing assessment → LOW-MEDIUM; combined gaps elevate overall risk to upper MEDIUM.
recommendations: Obtain the latest RTC (Pahani) to confirm actual extent, kharab area, and current cultivation status
Cross-verify ownership through Mutation Register (MR), Index of Lands, and 15-year RTC history
Request a Tippani and Hissa Phodi sketch to confirm the physical boundaries of Hissa No. 1
Conduct a survey department verification to reconcile missing Akarband fields
Obtain an Encumbrance Certificate (EC) for at least 30 years before purchase
Engage a licensed surveyor for on-ground measurement before executing a sale deed
llm_risk.summary: Survey No. 117/1 in Hupuha village is classified as Dry (private agricultural) land, which is favorable. However, critical Akarband fields — total extent, cultivable area, kharab, assessment, and owner name — are all blank. This incomplete record creates MEDIUM buyer risk due to the inability to verify area, ownership, and revenue liability. Proceed only after corroborating with RTC, Mutation, EC, and a physical survey.
